purpose: Producer-delta audit for rust-sdk-generator#158. This is intentionally not the adapter-supported call-shape matrix owned by #155.

audited.reproduction: The workflow .github/workflows/fork-manifest-removal-evidence.yml checks out all immutable revisions, generates and compares ordinary Rust and compiles the manifest-free facade.

classification.B: shared generator refactor/naming/signature logic required by A

repeated_nullable_multipart.title: [bug]: Handle repeated scalar and nullable binary multipart fields
repeated_nullable_multipart.note: Upstream issue creation was attempted on 2026-09-21 but the GitHub integration returned HTTP 403; the generic issue draft is in UPSTREAM_HANDOFF.md.

capabilities.emitted_rust_difference: Typed multipart generation unwraps a single non-null anyOf branch, recognizes nullable referenced binary schemas as binary parts, recognizes arrays of scalar/string-enum values, and emits one form.text(wire_name, item.to_string()) call per array item.
capabilities.observable_user_behavior: Repeated scalar multipart values are transmitted as repeated fields and optional nullable binary uploads remain binary multipart Parts instead of falling into an unsupported shape.

unmodified_upstream_equivalent.evidence: Pinned upstream and fork generated outputs are contrasted on the generic multipart fixture in fork-manifest-removal-evidence.yml; upstream lacks the emitted repeated-form loop, while fork emits it. The fork fixture also exercises a nullable referenced binary field.

generic_openapi_shapes: multipart/form-data object property with type=array and scalar/string-enum items
binary property wrapped by anyOf[$ref(binary), null]

manifest_free_adapter.evidence: This changes request-body construction only; canonical extraction consumes the ordinary generated method/signature and exact effective OpenAPI and requires no producer manifest field for this encoding.

capabilities.emitted_rust_difference: Multipart operations keep the historical method and add a collision-safe helper accepting multipart_filenames: &[(&str, &str)]; binary parts lookup overrides by OpenAPI wire name and call Part::file_name only when supplied.
capabilities.observable_user_behavior: Each request can attach independent filenames to multiple binary fields without mutable HttpClient state and without changing the base method wire behavior.

unmodified_upstream_equivalent.evidence: The pinned upstream ordinary client omits the request-local filename helper on the identical generic multipart fixture while the fork emits it; issue #77 requests the feature.

generic_openapi_shapes: multipart/form-data request with one or more format=binary fields

manifest_free_adapter.evidence: PR #159 requires direct AST/body proof that the helper consumes multipart_filenames, matches field names and calls .file_name; no manifest is needed.

capabilities.emitted_rust_difference: Generated client exposes HttpResponseByteStream as BoxStream<'static, Result<Bytes, reqwest::Error>> on native and LocalBoxStream<'static, ...> on wasm, and returns Box::pin(response.bytes_stream()).
capabilities.observable_user_behavior: Streaming methods expose a named owned 'static ABI that can outlive the response-local borrow and is portable across native and wasm Send requirements.

unmodified_upstream_equivalent.evidence: #148 generated an SSE-only fixture from pinned upstream and observed an anonymous impl Stream return. Upstream has SSE transport work, but the pinned ordinary client does not expose the fork's named native/wasm owned ABI.

generic_openapi_shapes: successful text/event-stream response

manifest_free_adapter.evidence: PR #159 accepts streams only when ordinary Rust proves both native and wasm aliases, item/error types and 'static lifetime.

capabilities.emitted_rust_difference: For binary successful representations the client emits an additive live-stream method backed by response.bytes_stream() while retaining the buffered call shape.
capabilities.observable_user_behavior: Large application/octet-stream or other binary responses can be consumed incrementally instead of fully buffering the successful body.

unmodified_upstream_equivalent.evidence: Pinned upstream does not emit the live binary stream call shape; upstream issue #78 explicitly requests it.

generic_openapi_shapes: successful binary response such as application/octet-stream with string/binary schema

manifest_free_adapter.evidence: PRs #154/#159 recover binary_stream from emitted behavior plus the owned stream ABI and fail closed on anonymous/ambiguous streams.

capabilities.emitted_rust_difference: No standalone public method is added by this commit; analysis retains all declared success response transport/media representations instead of collapsing immediately to one preferred representation.
capabilities.observable_user_behavior: Enables later raw generation to expose otherwise-lost JSON/SSE/binary alternatives from one operation.

unmodified_upstream_equivalent.evidence: #148 generated a JSON+SSE operation from pinned upstream and observed only the JSON call shape.

generic_openapi_shapes: one operation/status with multiple response media types
representations distributed across multiple successful statuses

manifest_free_adapter.evidence: The adapter consumes emitted call shapes, not this internal producer inventory.

capabilities.emitted_rust_difference: A shared pre-render planner allocates collision-safe method names, representation identity, success statuses/types and additional representation-specific call shapes; source rendering consumes that plan.
capabilities.observable_user_behavior: Operations can expose distinct generated methods for alternate buffered/SSE/binary representations with consistent status handling and method-name allocation.

unmodified_upstream_equivalent.evidence: #148's pinned-upstream JSON+SSE fixture emitted only the preferred JSON method; issue #78 tracks multiple representations.

generic_openapi_shapes: multiple successful response media types
multiple successful status codes with differing representations

manifest_free_adapter.evidence: The adapter does not consume the planner API; it independently recovers the resulting ordinary Rust methods and validates their status/media semantics.

capabilities.emitted_rust_difference: Configured representation-specific request discriminator rules are validated against one typed request model and emitted as direct field assignments before request serialization; planning retains the exact field/value projection.
capabilities.observable_user_behavior: A generated call shape can force the request field value required to select the corresponding server-side response mode while failing closed on ambiguous, optional-body or incompatible field rules.

unmodified_upstream_equivalent.evidence: Pinned upstream has no equivalent client.request_discriminators configuration or emitted assignment behavior.

generic_openapi_shapes: required typed request body with a scalar/enum discriminator field
one source operation exposing multiple configured response representations

manifest_free_adapter.evidence: PR #159 proves the direct assignment in the emitted method body and correlates it to the exact OpenAPI request field; it rejects defaults/comments/OpenAPI-only declarations.

upstream_work.note: Keep fork-only for now: this is generic producer policy but is not implied by OpenAPI itself, so no upstream issue was opened as part of #158.

capabilities.emitted_rust_difference: Collision suffixes for inline client parameter enum variants are emitted as PascalCase identifiers such as Created2 instead of Created_2 while preserving serde wire names.
capabilities.observable_user_behavior: Generated parameter enum names stay idiomatic and stable when values such as created and -created normalize to the same Rust variant base.

unmodified_upstream_equivalent.evidence: The same generic parameter-enum fixture emits the upstream collision suffix Created_2 and fork suffix Created2; upstream PR #19 addressed broader collision handling, not this specific spelling.

capabilities.emitted_rust_difference: Manifest work refactored existing source rendering to share return-signature and enum/union/parameter-enum naming plans; those helpers still drive ordinary Rust and are intentionally retained when manifest serialization is deleted.
capabilities.observable_user_behavior: No new standalone capability; retaining these helpers prevents output drift between the pre-removal and post-removal fork.

unmodified_upstream_equivalent.evidence: This is fork-internal factoring around fork-only raw generation.

upstream_work.note: Do not upstream manifest-driven factoring as a rust-sdk-generator requirement. Individual generic behavior belongs with the raw capabilities it supports.
